newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds end mixed in high volume.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds end mixed in high volume.

text.p: Israeli bond prices closed mixed on Thursday on very high turnover as most of the activity was concentrated in bonds linked to the consumer price index.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.13 pct to 167.63
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.08 pct at 161.49
Volume was very high at 235 million shekels with the linked bonds falling for the first time in two weeks, traders said.

"Despite the high activity in the linked bonds they fell for the first time in two weeks. Those bonds rose very fast during the last two months with yields falling from a peak of 5.25 percent to 4.5 percent," said Gidi Halperin at Meitav Investments.
Halperin added that the linked bonds were also affected by an announcement ot the Bank of Israel that it will issue new linked bonds.
"The main reason for the decline in the linked bonds was that investors took profit after the sharp rise in recent weeks," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeler Eblgon Securities.
The dollar linked bonds declined mildly despite another decline of the shekel. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2730 shekels against 3.2670 on Wednesday.
"The dollar linked bonds never react immediately to changes in the forex trading. It will probably affect trading only on Sunday," Halperin said.
The unlinked bonds and the Makams were the only gainers today.

"The unlinked bonds rose because they were offering a high yield of 16.7 percent. The provident funds were also buying bonds today as they are trying to show improved results at the end of the month," Eidelheit added.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
